boundary.rationale: Extraction area = world agent bbox from cities.js BUC_DISTRICTS (so every street the world builds is covered). Hexagon ~1.3 km E-W: west edge just past Piața Unirii (Dâmbovița/Splaiul, Dealul Mitropoliei foot), south edge Bd. Unirii + one block (Str. Radu Vodă / Splaiul Unirii quiet), north edge one block past Calea Călărașilor (Str. Popa Soare/Mihăileanu, quiet), east edge Str. Traian + Hala Traian; cut corners (SE Văcărești, NW Lipscani) keep it ≈1.1 km².

chapters.why: Start on the west side of Piața Unirii by the Dâmbovița (Fântâna lui Bucur fountain field on the left, Dealul Mitropoliei ahead) → round the south side → Bd. research.cross_section: Communist-era showpiece (1984–89, "Victoria Socialismului"), 92 m wide between facades: two one-way carriageways of 3 lanes each (60 km/h) either side of a wide central reservation holding the fountain basins in a long chain (east part continues to ~Bd. Mircea Vodă/Nerva Traian), lawns and linden rows; generous 8–10 m sidewalks with grey pavers, kerbside lindens; restaurant pavilions/terraces (Aici, Altfel, Jo Lounge, Naked Kitchen, Moon, The Clique) along the south side east of the square
research.frontage: continuous 8–10-storey 1980s Civic-Centre apartment blocks with ground-floor arcades, cream/ochre stone & render facades (#D8CDB5–#C9B99A), dark-wood/aluminium windows, balcony rows, pitched/mansard metal roofs with decorative cornices; rooftop advertising letters on several blocks

research.layout: Largest square in central Bucharest; one-way gyratory system (3–9 lane approaches with heavy turn channelisation) around a central park with the fountain field; the square is a concrete slab ("Planșeul Unirii", 32 × 360 m) over the Dâmbovița, which runs diagonally underneath; Bd. Unirii crosses W–E; Pasajul Unirii road underpass N–S (I.C. Brătianu ↔ Cantemir); Piața Unirii metro (M1/M2/M3, Unirii 1 & 2) with many entrances; tram terminal near the SW corner; big taxi rank
research.fountains: see top-level `fountains` (layout, basins, jets, lighting, show schedule)
research.park: lawns, rose beds, linden & birch groups, benches; the round central fountain basin (OSM n1423222582 "Fântâna lui Bucur")
research.frontage: E: Unirea Shopping Center (1976, enlarged 1989; 6 levels in OSM, long horizontal facade with ad banners) + Hala Unirii + Parcare Unirea deck; N: Hanul lui Manuc (1808) near NE corner, Old Town edge; S/SW: Dealul Mitropoliei with the Patriarchal Cathedral on the hill, Sf. Spiridon Nou church (Cantemir); 1980s Civic-Centre blocks (8–10 storeys, cream/beige stone-clad, arcaded ground floors, mansard-like roofs) on all corners carrying large rooftop advertising letters/LED screens
research.works_2023_2026: Since 2023 vehicles >3.5 t are banned on the slab; reconstruction of the Dâmbovița cover started 2024–25 and was in its final stage in summer 2026 (>60 % done, expected end-2026) with restrictions around Pasajul Unirii. Recommendation: model the finished/normal layout (the CV chapter is 2015) and optionally add hoardings at the Pasaj.

research.cross_section: two-way 2+2 (3+2 near junctions), 50 km/h, trolleybus 73 wires, buses 116/117/312/323/385
research.frontage: W: Day Tower (37A, 9 lv, 2018 glass office, Starbucks ground floor), Mercure hotel (28, 12 lv, 2006), Hotel Marina; E: 9-storey 1980s blocks E1/E2 and new 21D Downtown residences (9 lv, 2016), BCR & BRD branches, Sector 3 civil-status office

research.cross_section: TWO-WAY 1+1 (≈7–8 m carriageway), 50 km/h, asphalt with patches; cars parked half on the narrow (1.5–2.5 m) sidewalks on both sides; no tram/trolley on this stretch; overhead telecom cables and older concrete lamp poles
research.frontage: Bucharest's best-preserved row of late-19th/early-20th-c. merchant houses ("case de târgoveț"): 1–2-storey rendered street houses (nos. 78–111 listed LMI B-II-m-B-183xx, built 1900–1920) with tall windows, pilasters, cornices, carriage gates, many shabby or seismic-risk; interspersed with 4–6-storey interwar blocks (no. 105, 1936; 117-119 S+P+4+attic) and a few 1990s infills; >200 legally protected buildings along the street
research.hala_traian: no. 133 at the Traian corner: Hala Traian (1896) — one of the last two 19th-c. market halls; cream facade with red-brick bands and a big arched window, small shops (red fascia, blue PESCĂRIE) in the front, supermarket inside; Piața Traian open market opposite (south side). Trams stop right at the junction (stop "Hala Traian", platforms with red-white painted kerbs, trolley/tram wires overhead) — photos 2019–2022
research.businesses: Mega Image (133), Superbet, Farmacia Dona, myGOLD & Tezaur pawn shops, shaorma, pastry shop, car-parts shops, Bulgust, Toka, Tripoli restaurants (OSM)

top_local_details: Piața Unirii is a vast square on a slab over the Dâmbovița — fountains, park, gyratory, metro, Unirea mall on the east side.

Fountains continue as a long chain of alternating long/short basins in the Bd. Unirii median; the square has big rectangular basins around a round central fountain; Simfonia Apei shows Fri–Sun 21:00 May–Sept.
Bd. Unirii = 1980s Champs-Élysées copy: uniform 8–10-storey cream/ochre blocks with arcades and decorative rooflines; Palace of the Parliament closes the vista west.
Bd. Unirii carriageways are one-way 3-lane each side of the fountain median.
Rooftop advertising letters and LED screens on the blocks around Piața Unirii.
Unirea Shopping Center: long 1970s facade with brand banners, partly empty windows on the north side.
Dealul Mitropoliei with the Patriarchal Cathedral visible from the square.
Calea Călărașilor is a narrow TWO-WAY street, nothing like a boulevard.
Calea Călărașilor is lined by low 1900–1920 merchant houses (listed), many shabby, with a few 1930s 6-storey blocks.
Cars parked on the sidewalks of Calea Călărașilor; loose overhead cables.
Hala Traian (1896): cream facade striped with red brick, big arched window, small shop fascias; supermarket inside.

culture_notes.note: "Bună ziua" with strangers, "Salut/Neața" among young people; "dumneavoastră" (formal you) to older people; "Mersi" is as common as "Mulțumesc".
Bucharest drivers honk readily and often do not stop at zebras; pedestrians answer with sarcasm rather than aggression — keep lines teasing, not violent.
Cars parked on sidewalks are a constant pedestrian complaint; a natural topic for bumped/idle lines in side streets.
At OTP passengers order licensed taxis from touch-screen kiosks in Arrivals; unsolicited offers are a known nuisance — staff lines should point to the kiosks.
Personas are defined by role/place (student, vendor, commuter), never by ethnicity; Roma, Moldovan or diaspora characters are not caricatured; humour targets traffic, weather, parking and the metro.

fountains.name: Fântânile Urbane din Piața Unirii (Urban Fountains of Unirii Square) — show "Simfonia Apei"
fountains.summary: 44 independent, individually controllable fountains along almost 1.4 km of Bd. Unirii + Piața Unirii, ≈16,200 m² of water surface; built late 1980s (Civic Centre), rehabilitated by Apa Nova with the city for ≈€7 M and reopened Sept 2018 with a digitally controlled water-music-light system; certified 2019 by the World Record Academy as the longest synchronised choreographed fountain array. OSM maps 45 basins in the extraction area (10 on Bd. Unirii west of the square, 25 in the square, 10 east) — matching the official 44 + the small amenity=fountain w413969309.

layout.square: symmetric field centred on the round central fountain (OSM node "Fântâna lui Bucur", 44.42678, 26.10246) in the middle of the park: two rows (N and S of the Bd. Unirii axis) of large rectangular basins ~48×35 m (≈1,000 m² each, w1128204286/287/292/293) flanked by ~34×31 m basins (≈630 m²) and ~31×18 m end basins (≈450 m²), separated by paved promenades; thin 1–2 m wide water channels (w1176142645 etc.) link them; basins are shallow (OSM height 0.4 m rim) with grey stone/concrete coping
layout.boulevard: a single line of basins in the central reservation of Bd. Unirii, alternating long 28×7 m basins (~11 jet nodes each) and short 13×6 m basins (~3 jets) at ≈37 m pitch, running west towards Piața Constituției/the Parliament and east to ≈26.110 (Bd. Mircea Vodă); lawns, low hedges and linden rows either side of the basins

fountains.jets: per basin: lines of vertical jets in the long basins, central tall jet + ring in the large square basins, arching/rotating "Vario" jet groups; ~374 jet/nozzle points mapped as amenity=fountain nodes in OSM (use as nozzle positions); show jets reach ~10–15 m in the square (estimate from photos; no official figure found), boulevard jets 2–6 m
fountains.lighting: underwater RGB LED projectors in every basin; colour-cycling on show nights, static white/blue after sunset otherwise; street lamps + ad screens around the square add warm/white light

show.name: Simfonia Apei (Water Symphony)
show.season: May → end of September (2025: 23 May – 28 Sept, weekly)
show.content: water choreography synchronised to music (themes change yearly — 2024 film themes; special editions with drone shows, e.g. Olympic tribute) + lights; crowds of families line the basins, ~200,000 spectators over the first 70 shows
show.game_rule: if local time is Fri–Sun, May–Sept, 21:00–21:45 → run the show (jets animate to music, LEDs cycle); otherwise jets run in a calm daytime pattern 10:00–23:00 and are off at night/in winter (basins drained Nov–Apr).

fountains.status_2025_2026: The 2025 season was cut short: shows only until the end of June 2025, then the fountains in the square were decommissioned for the Planșeul Unirii slab reconstruction (final stage summer 2026, completion expected end-2026). For the 2015 chapter / free drive render the full working fountains.
